Your 1,000-hour journey

Ten stages × ten units × ten hours = 1,000 hours. Units include lesson study, independent input, vocabulary, use, and review. Exact CEFR progress varies by learner. At ten hours weekly this is about 100 weeks; at fifteen, about 67; at twenty, 50.

Stage map

Section titled “Stage map”
Stage Working level Hours Main work
1 A0–A1 1–100 Sounds, sense, and first conversations
2 A1 101–200 Everyday sentences
3 A2 201–300 Time and movement
4 A2–B1 301–400 Telling a story
5 B1 401–500 Decisions and relationships
6 B1–B2 501–600 Mood and complex ideas
7 B2 601–700 Argument and precise prose
8 B2 701–800 Register, cohesion, and literary reading
9 C1 801–900 Academic and professional French
10 C1 901–1000 C1 integration and independent mastery

01 · Sounds, sense, and first conversations

Section titled “01 · Sounds, sense, and first conversations”

1.1 · First meeting · hours 1–10

Section titled “1.1 · First meeting · hours 1–10”

Outcome: Introduce yourself and use a repair phrase.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s first meeting material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.2 · Vowel contrasts · hours 11–20

Section titled “1.2 · Vowel contrasts · hours 11–20”

Outcome: Distinguish /u/ and /y/ and recognize common nasal vowels.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s vowel contrasts material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.3 · Consonants and rhythm · hours 21–30

Section titled “1.3 · Consonants and rhythm · hours 21–30”

Outcome: Read short phrases with meaningful grouping.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s consonants and rhythm material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.4 · Noun phrases · hours 31–40

Section titled “1.4 · Noun phrases · hours 31–40”

Outcome: Use articles and basic gender agreement.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s noun phrases material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.5 · Subjects and être · hours 41–50

Section titled “1.5 · Subjects and être · hours 41–50”

Outcome: Build accurate identity and location sentences.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s subjects and être material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.6 · Avoir and personal details · hours 51–60

Section titled “1.6 · Avoir and personal details · hours 51–60”

Outcome: Give age, possession, and basic needs.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s avoir and personal details material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.7 · Questions and repair · hours 61–70

Section titled “1.7 · Questions and repair · hours 61–70”

Outcome: Ask and answer predictable polite questions.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s questions and repair material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.8 · Time and appointments · hours 71–80

Section titled “1.8 · Time and appointments · hours 71–80”

Outcome: Arrange and confirm a simple appointment.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s time and appointments material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.9 · Reading and retelling · hours 81–90

Section titled “1.9 · Reading and retelling · hours 81–90”

Outcome: Extract the message from a short French introduction.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s reading and retelling material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

1.10 · First conversation portfolio · hours 91–100

Section titled “1.10 · First conversation portfolio · hours 91–100”

Outcome: Complete a short introduction and interaction with reflection.

  • Read and work through Chapter 1’s first conversation portfolio material (2h).
  • Focused listening and pronunciation (2h); vocabulary and spaced review (2h).
  • Interaction or recorded speaking (2h); reading and writing (1h); exercises and reflection (1h).

02 · Everyday sentences

Section titled “02 · Everyday sentences”

2.1 · Articles and household objects · hours 101–110

Section titled “2.1 · Articles and household objects · hours 101–110”

Outcome: Introduce objects with accurate gender and article.

  • Label twenty objects with articles and gender.
  • Write ten c’est introductions and plural versions.
  • Record a one-minute room tour, then correct it.

2.2 · Plural phrases and a neighborhood · hours 111–120

Section titled “2.2 · Plural phrases and a neighborhood · hours 111–120”

Outcome: Describe several places and objects.

  • Turn fifteen singular descriptions into plurals.
  • Listen for le, la, and les before checking text.
  • Create a neighborhood inventory and describe it aloud.

2.3 · Adjectives and descriptions · hours 121–130

Section titled “2.3 · Adjectives and descriptions · hours 121–130”

Outcome: Match adjective forms to nouns and compare positions.

  • Write twenty adjective phrases with justified agreement.
  • Contrast un ancien collègue and un meuble ancien.
  • Describe two people and two places without a script.

2.4 · Family and possession · hours 131–140

Section titled “2.4 · Family and possession · hours 131–140”

Outcome: Identify relationships with possessives and demonstratives.

  • Draw a fictional family and colleague map.
  • Practice son amie versus sa sœur in context.
  • Write and record ten relationship captions.

2.5 · Regular present and routines · hours 141–150

Section titled “2.5 · Regular present and routines · hours 141–150”

Outcome: Explain a weekday routine in the present.

  • Conjugate regular verbs inside routine sentences.
  • Interview a partner about five habits.
  • Revise a 120-word weekday routine.

2.6 · Être, avoir, aller, faire · hours 151–160

Section titled “2.6 · Être, avoir, aller, faire · hours 151–160”

Outcome: Express age, needs, destinations, and common actions.

  • Retrieve être, avoir, aller, faire with varied subjects.
  • Solve a weekly schedule task orally.
  • State age, needs, location, and destination in one exchange.

2.7 · Modals and pronominal verbs · hours 161–170

Section titled “2.7 · Modals and pronominal verbs · hours 161–170”

Outcome: Describe self-care and what a person can or must do.

  • Build a morning sequence with pronominal verbs.
  • Make plans with pouvoir, vouloir, devoir plus infinitive.
  • Shadow a routine and rerecord after comparison.

2.8 · Negatives and preferences · hours 171–180

Section titled “2.8 · Negatives and preferences · hours 171–180”

Outcome: Deny possession, preference, and routine precisely.

  • Contrast pas, jamais, and plus using a schedule.
  • Negate indefinite possession and generic preference.
  • Complete a listening grid before viewing the transcript.

2.9 · Questions, numbers, appointments · hours 181–190

Section titled “2.9 · Questions, numbers, appointments · hours 181–190”

Outcome: Ask for information and arrange a meeting.

  • Ask a question with each major question word.
  • Dictate prices, dates, and meeting times.
  • Arrange three meetings with day, time, and place.

2.10 · Welcome-pack project · hours 191–200

Section titled “2.10 · Welcome-pack project · hours 191–200”

Outcome: Integrate an introduction, neighborhood, routine, and invitation.

  • Write a 150–180-word welcome pack.
  • Record a two-minute introduction and answer follow-ups.
  • Complete mixed practice and revise the three main error patterns.

03 · Time and movement

Section titled “03 · Time and movement”

3.1 · Past events with avoir · hours 201–210

Section titled “3.1 · Past events with avoir · hours 201–210”

Outcome: Build a completed past event with an auxiliary and participle.

  • Place purchases and journeys on a timeline.
  • Build ten avoir-based event reports.
  • Dictate auxiliaries and participles in complete sentences.

3.2 · Irregular participles · hours 211–220

Section titled “3.2 · Irregular participles · hours 211–220”

Outcome: Retrieve frequent participles inside practical messages.

  • Retrieve fait, pris, vu, lu, écrit, dit, mis, eu, été, bu.
  • Write a short travel message with five irregular participles.
  • Correct infinitive-versus-participle errors with reasons.

3.3 · Past events with être · hours 221–230

Section titled “3.3 · Past events with être · hours 221–230”

Outcome: Choose an auxiliary by verb construction and apply agreement.

  • Contrast elle est sortie and elle a sorti les clés.
  • Report a journey with aller, arriver, partir, and rester.
  • Explain silent subject agreement in a written account.

3.4 · A lost-property report · hours 231–240

Section titled “3.4 · A lost-property report · hours 231–240”

Outcome: Report when, where, what happened, and what help is needed.

  • Write a lost-property report with location and time.
  • Describe a missing object without private identifying data.
  • Role-play a request for help and a clarification.

3.5 · Plans with aller · hours 241–250

Section titled “3.5 · Plans with aller · hours 241–250”

Outcome: Make and explain a coherent future plan.

  • Create a weekend itinerary with aller plus infinitive.
  • Add negative plans and reflexive activities.
  • Interview a partner about a contingency.

3.6 · Simple future and contingencies · hours 251–260

Section titled “3.6 · Simple future and contingencies · hours 251–260”

Outcome: Announce a future event and give a conditional alternative.

  • Build future stems and endings with varied subjects.
  • Contrast quand tu arriveras and si tu arrives.
  • Write a confirmation and a weather alternative.

3.7 · Directions and imperatives · hours 261–270

Section titled “3.7 · Directions and imperatives · hours 261–270”

Outcome: Give and follow clear instructions.

  • Give a route with four recognizable landmarks.
  • Contrast affirmative and negative commands.
  • Follow a spoken route before checking its written version.

3.8 · Food, quantities, and shopping · hours 271–280

Section titled “3.8 · Food, quantities, and shopping · hours 271–280”

Outcome: Request food and amounts within constraints.

  • Distinguish a countable unit from an unspecified amount.
  • Buy food within a budget and request an alternative.
  • Dictate quantities and payment details.

3.9 · Objects, transport, and duration · hours 281–290

Section titled “3.9 · Objects, transport, and duration · hours 281–290”

Outcome: Avoid repeated objects and preserve time relationships.

  • Replace definite direct objects with le, la, les.
  • Practice téléphoner à with lui and leur.
  • Contrast depuis, pendant, il y a, and dans on a timeline.

3.10 · A three-day trip dossier · hours 291–300

Section titled “3.10 · A three-day trip dossier · hours 291–300”

Outcome: Integrate plans, transactions, directions, and a past report.

  • Write a 180-word itinerary and shopping list.
  • Record directions and respond to a disrupted plan.
  • Write a 180-word completed-trip report and review four dimensions.

04 · Telling a story

Section titled “04 · Telling a story”

4.1 · Forming the imparfait · hours 301–310

Section titled “4.1 · Forming the imparfait · hours 301–310”

Outcome: Build imparfait forms from present nous stems.

  • Build imparfait stems from ten present nous forms.
  • Explain être’s exceptional stem and spelling changes.
  • Write and record a past routine.

4.2 · Background and completed events · hours 311–320

Section titled “4.2 · Background and completed events · hours 311–320”

Outcome: Use viewpoint to distinguish background and bounded events.

  • Contrast a closed ten-year period with a background residence.
  • Revise an event list into a coherent account.
  • Justify five tense choices using event relationships.

4.3 · Habits and interrupted activities · hours 321–330

Section titled “4.3 · Habits and interrupted activities · hours 321–330”

Outcome: Explain past routines and overlapping events.

  • Describe childhood holidays and repeated habits.
  • Contrast simultaneous activity with sequential actions.
  • Dictate a narrative and reconstruct its timeline.

4.4 · The earlier past · hours 331–340

Section titled “4.4 · The earlier past · hours 331–340”

Outcome: Place one past event before another.

  • Compare she left at arrival with she had already left.
  • Explain a missed train using an earlier cause.
  • Retell one event in chronological and explanatory order.

4.5 · Direct and indirect objects · hours 341–350

Section titled “4.5 · Direct and indirect objects · hours 341–350”

Outcome: Follow French verb frames to replace objects.

  • Classify objects using French verb constructions.
  • Replace repeated noun phrases with direct or indirect pronouns.
  • Compare parler à, parler de, and penser à with people.

4.6 · Y and en in context · hours 351–360

Section titled “4.6 · Y and en in context · hours 351–360”

Outcome: Track places, selected complements, and quantities.

  • Replace places and selected à-complements with y.
  • Replace quantities and selected de-complements with en.
  • Explain definite les billets versus indefinite des billets.

4.7 · Two pronouns and agreement · hours 361–370

Section titled “4.7 · Two pronouns and agreement · hours 361–370”

Outcome: Order compatible pronouns and justify common participle agreement.

  • Build a two-pronoun sentence from a full noun phrase.
  • Contrast affirmative and negative imperatives.
  • Correct trouvé/trouvées and lavées/lavé les mains by role analysis.

4.8 · Relative clauses · hours 371–380

Section titled “4.8 · Relative clauses · hours 371–380”

Outcome: Connect information with qui, que, où, and dont.

  • Combine short sentences with each major relative.
  • Reconstruct the underlying sentences to identify roles.
  • Write a description with clear antecedents and no redundant de after dont.

4.9 · Comparisons and administration · hours 381–390

Section titled “4.9 · Comparisons and administration · hours 381–390”

Outcome: Compare options and complete a clear administrative request.

  • Compare two routes, rooms, or services using meilleur and mieux.
  • Write a fictional document request and attachment message.
  • Role-play a missing-document problem and clarify the next step.
